dossier.purpose: Dagu is a local-first workflow engine: YAML-defined DAGs of shell commands, containers, SSH/HTTP and other built-in actions, executed by a single Go binary that also provides the CLI, an embedded React Web UI, a REST API, an MCP endpoint, a cron/queue scheduler, retries, and file-backed run history with no external database or broker (README.md:18-20; ARCHITECTURE.md:7-33). An optional gRPC coordinator plus workers distribute runs (README.md:224-228). Surface relevant to scheduled local runs: `dagu start-all` or `dagu scheduler` for scheduling; `dagu start|stop|retry|enqueue|status|history|ps` and the Web UI for supervision. The docs site (docs.dagu.sh) that the README links throughout is not part of the checkout (no docs/ directory) and was not read.

claims.claim: Dagu is a local-first workflow engine for operations and internal automation: a single binary with a built-in Web UI, no external database or message broker, on Linux, macOS and Windows.
Turns existing scripts and runbooks into production workflows with scheduling, retries, human tasks and run history; runs on-prem, air-gapped, edge or cloud.
Run existing shell commands, Docker containers, Kubernetes Jobs and remote SSH commands without modifications.
Schedule workflows with cron syntax, timezones, overlap policies and catch-up windows.
Keep logs, run history, retries, notifications and webhook triggers in one place.
Overlap policies: skip (default: skip if previous run is still active), all (queue all), latest (keep only the most recent); catch-up automatically runs missed intervals when the scheduler was down.
Zombie detection identifies and handles stalled DAG runs (configurable interval, default 45s).
Per-step retry policies with limits, intervals and exit-code filtering; lifecycle hooks (onInit/onSuccess/onFailure/onAbort/onExit/onWait); preconditions.
High availability: scheduler lock with stale detection for failover.
`dagu start-all` runs the server, scheduler, and steps in one process on one machine.

A single machine can run thousands of workflow runs per day (capacity depends on CPU, memory, disk, workflow shape); queues, concurrency limits and resource limits control how many runs execute at once and where.
Built-in MCP server at http://localhost:8080/mcp: inspect workflows and runs, maintain Wiki pages, apply changes, control runs through the same authenticated boundary as the REST API.
With builtin auth, five roles (admin, manager, developer, operator, viewer) control access; API keys have independent roles; audit logging tracks all actions.
Community self-host needs no license key; a self-host license adds SSO, RBAC, audit logging and incident SaaS integration.

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - release archives for linux/amd64 (.goreleaser.yaml:14-19), unit and integration tests on ubuntu-latest in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:185-200), installer handles x86_64 (scripts/installer.sh:617-631), linux/amd64 Docker image (.github/workflows/docker.yaml:29-33).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL/WSL2 mention anywhere in the repo (repo-wide search); Linux binaries exist, but WSL2 is neither documented nor exercised in CI.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - darwin/arm64 archives (.goreleaser.yaml:14-22), npm package dagu-darwin-arm64 (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yaml:62-65), installer writes a user LaunchAgent (scripts/installer.sh:1740-1837). Caveats: CI has no macOS test job (tests run on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest only: ci.yaml:185-189,631-635; macOS appears only as a GOOS=darwin lint at ci.yaml:150 and an npm install smoke test at npm-publish.yaml:277-282); `resources.limits` are not enforced on macOS (internal/runtime/resourcelimit/native_unsupported.go:14-16); config dir is fixed to ~/.config (internal/cmn/config/loader.go:185-188) while data/log dirs come from adrg/xdg DataHome (loader.go:186), so the macOS data location may differ from the README's Linux defaults (library behaviour not verified).
platforms.gpu: no - no GPU detection, scheduling or accounting in the code; only user-defined worker labels (for example gpu=true) used for routing (README.md:794,804; internal/cmd/worker.go:52). The Helm chart README shows nvidia.com/gpu requests for worker pools (charts/dagu/README.md:216-232).

integrations.cli: Yes. The `dagu` binary registers 33 subcommands (cmd/main.go:36-68) including start, start-all, scheduler, server, stop, restart, retry, enqueue/dequeue, status, history, ls, ps, validate, dry, cleanup, schema, example, upgrade, exec. README lists 18 'common' commands and says 31 total (README.md:811-832). A persistent `--context` flag targets a remote Dagu server's API (cmd/main.go:35; internal/cmd/context_command.go:43).
integrations.mcp: Yes. Built-in MCP server, Streamable HTTP only (no stdio transport found), at `<base>/mcp` of the Dagu server, registered on every server start (internal/service/mcp/server.go:58-65; internal/service/frontend/server.go:896,1345-1363). Tools: dagu_read, dagu_change (preview/apply), dagu_execute (start/enqueue/retry/stop) (server.go:26-28,113-154); `dagu://` resources; auth follows the server auth mode and API keys need the `mcp` surface (specs/020-mcp-server.md:37-73). specs/020-mcp-server.md:3 says Draft and specs/README.md:31 lists it as 'Not implemented'.
integrations.sdk_or_api: REST API: OpenAPI 3.0.0 at api/v1/api.yaml (173 paths, 230 operationIds; server base /api/v1, api.yaml:2,14-16), Go server code generated into api/v1/api.gen.go; SSE streams back the UI. Embedded Go API: root package github.com/dagucloud/dagu/v2, explicitly experimental (doc.go:4-9; README.md:1010-1047; examples/embedded); embedding in a distributed binary carries GPL obligations (LICENSING.md:7-13). No other-language SDKs found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: (1) A bundled `dagu` agent skill (skills/dagu/SKILL.md; skills/README.md:3-6) that the installer can place into detected Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex (~/.codex or ~/.agents), OpenCode, Gemini and Copilot locations via `gh skill install dagucloud/dagu dagu` or `npx skills add https://github.com/dagucloud/dagu --skill dagu` (scripts/installer.sh:634-655,2076-2105). (2) The `harness.run` action runs external coding-agent CLIs from DAG steps, including `claude -p` and `codex exec` (skills/dagu/references/harnesses.md:5-24; README.md:600). (3) AGENTS.md is a repository guide for coding agents (AGENTS.md:1-119). No Claude-Code-specific MCP configuration instructions were found (search for `claude mcp` / `.mcp.json` returned nothing).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No product-usage telemetry or analytics code found (repo-wide search for telemetry/analytics/posthog/sentry etc.). `internal/telemetry` is OpenTelemetry tracing that only activates when a DAG sets otel.enabled with an endpoint (internal/telemetry/tracer.go:42-45) plus a pull-based Prometheus collector whose endpoint access defaults to `private` (internal/service/frontend/server.go:316-321; internal/cmn/config/loader.go:2011). Outbound calls that do exist: (1) Update check, ON by default for the server process: queries https://api.github.com/repos/dagucloud/dagu/releases/latest at start and every 24h, skipped for dev builds, failures logged at debug; disable with `check_updates: false` / DAGU_CHECK_UPDATES (internal/service/frontend/server.go:916,1018-1045; internal/upgrade/cache.go:12-62; internal/upgrade/github.go:19,47-75; loader.go:1170,2009,2096; internal/service/frontend/file/stores.go:119-129; documented only in internal/cmn/schema/config.schema.json:37-41, not in the README). `dagu upgrade` is an explicit command (internal/cmd/upgrade.go:94-158). (2) Licensing, only when a key is configured: Dagu POSTs the key, a locally generated server ID, the hostname and the client version to https://console.dagu.sh and heartbeats every 24h; with no key it logs 'community mode' and makes no call; licence errors never block startup (internal/license/client.go:18,44-63,109; internal/license/manager.go:19-20,120-141,287-317,356-373). (3) Feature-specific: `tools:` provisioning via aqua and `action: owner/repo@version` packages fetched from GitHub (internal/tools/aqua/registryref.go:26; internal/runtime/builtin/action/resolver.go:295-304); LLM, browser, mail, S3 and similar steps contact whatever services they are configured for; the Tailscale tunnel is opt-in and off by default (loader.go:1642-1650). The Go-served page template references no external hosts (internal/service/frontend/templates/base.gohtml:1-78); the webpack HTML template ui/index.html:8-13 links Google Fonts (which one reaches a browser was not run). No account or hosted service is required for community use; a Dagu licence key (console.dagu.sh) is needed only for licensed features. Local listeners by default: HTTP 127.0.0.1:8080 (loader.go:2004-2005) and, under `start-all`, the coordinator gRPC on 127.0.0.1:50055, enabled by default with plaintext h2c (loader.go:1313-1321,2017-2019,2050; internal/cmd/startall.go:44-45). Step processes receive a filtered environment (PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, TERM, LANG, LC_*, TZ, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, XDG_*, DOCKER_* plus DAGU_/DAG_/LC_/KUBERNETES_ prefixes; extras via DAGU_ENV_PASSTHROUGH[_PREFIXES]) (internal/cmn/config/env.go:23-33,106-116; env_unix.go:16-49).

languages: Go (go.mod: go 1.27.0; 1,916 .go files including generated and test files)
PowerShell, CMD and Inno Setup (Windows installers)

entry_points.what: `dagu` binary: cobra root registering 33 subcommands (start, start-all, scheduler, server, coordinator, worker, stop, retry, enqueue, status, history, ...); version injected via -ldflags main.version (cmd/main.go:17-73).
`dagu start-all`: server + scheduler + (default-enabled) coordinator in one process; scheduler health server disabled in this mode (startall.go:99-253).
`dagu scheduler` foreground scheduler: tick planner, catch-up, queue processor, retry scanner, zombie detector, directory lock.
`dagu start <dag>` runs one DAG-run; the scheduler spawns this as a child process for each local scheduled run (launcher.go:134-135,457-488).
HTTP server: REST API (api/v1), SSE, embedded UI template/assets, /mcp route, optional web terminal, periodic update check.
MCP Streamable-HTTP handler exposing dagu_read / dagu_change / dagu_execute.

Linux/macOS installer wizard: downloads the release archive, verifies SHA-256 from checksums.txt, optionally writes a systemd unit or LaunchAgent running `dagu start-all` (installer.sh:1520-1546,1629-1698,1740-1837).

code.architecture: One Go module (github.com/dagucloud/dagu/v2) builds one binary holding every role. Pipeline: YAML -> internal/spec (decode/validate) -> internal/ir (canonical DAG + persisted run state) -> internal/intake (admission) -> internal/runtime (runner.go, node.go, plan.go; per-run agent in internal/runtime/agent/) -> executors in internal/runtime/builtin/ (registry in internal/executor/registry/) -> file persistence in internal/persis/file/ (ARCHITECTURE.md:7-33; AGENTS.md:13-50). Services: internal/service/frontend (HTTP API/SSE/embedded UI), internal/service/mcp, internal/service/scheduler (tick_planner.go, catchup.go, queue_processor.go, retry_scanner.go, zombie_detector.go), internal/service/coordinator + internal/service/worker (gRPC, proto/), internal/license, internal/upgrade, internal/telemetry. State is plain files under data_dir: per-run directories dag-run_* with dag.json and an append-only status.jsonl fsynced on each write (internal/persis/file/dagrun/dagrun.go:44-60; writer.go:81-104,148-164), proc heartbeat files (internal/persis/file/proc/store.go), queue and scheduler-state dirs (internal/persis/file/backend.go:38-71); the scheduler lock is a lock directory (internal/cmn/dirlock/dirlock.go). Execution model for a local scheduled run: the scheduler spawns `dagu start` as a child process (internal/service/scheduler/dag_executor.go:305-321; internal/launcher/launcher.go:134-135,500) in its own process group; each step command runs under cmdutil.StartManagedProcess (internal/runtime/builtin/command/command.go:105) with Setpgid and group-wide signals on Unix, a /bin/sh parent-exit watchdog that SIGKILLs the group if the run process dies (internal/cmn/cmdutil/cmd_unix.go:19-25; lifecycle_unix.go:33-57; parent_exit_watcher_unix.go:18-67) and Job Objects on Windows (lifecycle_windows.go:30-92). Cancellation: `dagu stop` reaches the live run via a local socket (internal/runtime/manager.go:83-215), sends the stop signal, resends every 5s and forces termination after max_clean_up_time_sec, default 5s (internal/runtime/agent/agent.go:2267-2341; internal/ir/dag.go:505-519). Specs live in specs/ with black-box tests in conformance/.
code.packaging_and_release: Tag-driven: release.yaml fires on v*.*.* tags, builds the UI with pnpm, then runs GoReleaser (.github/workflows/release.yaml:3-7,25-61). .goreleaser.yaml: CGO_ENABLED=0 archives for linux/darwin/windows x amd64/386/arm(v6,v7)/arm64/ppc64le/s390x (windows/arm excluded) (:8-35), checksums.txt SHA-256 list (:41-42), Homebrew formulae pushed to dagucloud/homebrew-brew and a deprecated yohamta/homebrew-tap, with a service block running `dagu start-all` (:54-88). Provenance: actions/attest records build provenance for the archives from dist/checksums.txt but is `continue-on-error: true` (release.yaml:63-71); a signed 'packslip' inventory (workflow-identity signing via jdx/packslip) is published for verifiers such as mise (release.yaml:73-110). No GPG/cosign signing of checksums.txt or images and no SBOM generation found in .goreleaser.yaml, release.yaml or docker.yaml. Other artifacts: Inno Setup Windows installer attached to the release (release.yaml:112-182); Docker images ghcr.io/dagucloud/dagu (latest, -dev, -alpine; linux/amd64, arm64, arm/v7) built on tags by docker.yaml (:3-41,84-86,156-176); npm @dagucloud/dagu plus 12 platform packages published with `npm publish --provenance` (npm-publish.yaml:42-101,192,258); Helm chart via chart-releaser to gh-pages (chart-release.yaml:41-50). Third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Source builds need the UI built and copied into internal/service/frontend/assets, which is git-ignored (.gitignore:3-4; Makefile:251-253,380-382; release.yaml:45-53). At this revision the Helm chart defaults its image tag to Chart.appVersion 2.11.1 (charts/dagu/Chart.yaml:5-7; values.yaml:13-17; templates/_helpers.tpl:46).
code.tests_and_ci: Go: testify + gotestsum (go.mod; Makefile:165-171). 941 *_test.go files of 1,916 Go files, including 114 under conformance/ (binary-level tests per spec, driven by DAGU_BIN; specs/README.md:95-102) and 84 under internal/intg/. About 319 test functions with names matching Schedul|Cron|Catchup|Overlap|Zombie|Stop|Cancel|Kill|Orphan|ParentExit across 118 files in internal/. 9 Benchmark functions in 5 files, no published results. UI: vitest (168 *.test.ts(x) files in ui/src) and Playwright e2e (15 specs in ui/e2e, including scheduler-recovery, zombie-recovery, worker-failover). Workflows in .github/workflows: ci.yaml (path-filtered; golangci-lint for linux/windows/darwin :140-183; go fmt / go fix checks; unit and integration suites in 3 shards each on ubuntu-latest with -race and Codecov upload, integration pre-pulls alpine/busybox/redis/minio images :185-284; compat job for OpenCode, GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2 and 386 jq :287-325; Playwright e2e in 3 shards :327-383; Windows installer tests :385-629; Windows unit+integration shards :631-686); conformance.yml (ubuntu + windows, 2 shards each, :45-105); frontend-ci.yaml (vitest + build); desktop-e2e.yaml (Windows desktop driver); docker-browser-smoke.yaml (dev image browser steps on amd64/arm64); image-security.yaml (Trivy image scan + govulncheck on PR/main and weekly cron, :28-29,69-78,94-103); chart-ci.yaml (helm lint/template/package); release.yaml, manual-release.yaml, docker.yaml, docker-manual.yaml, npm-publish.yaml, npm-publish-test.yaml, chart-release.yaml. No macOS test job. Dependabot: gomod/npm/actions monthly (patch-only groups, major/minor ignored), docker quarterly (.github/dependabot.yaml). Linting: golangci-lint v2 with gosec, staticcheck, errcheck, revive, exhaustive (.golangci.yml:4-22).
code.dependencies: go.mod (module github.com/dagucloud/dagu/v2, go 1.27.0): 97 direct requires + 447 indirect = 544 modules; no replace or tool directives. About 10 of the direct modules are dev tools pinned through tools.go (golangci-lint, gotestsum, oapi-codegen, protolint, golines, addlicense, changelog-from-release, protoc-gen-go and -go-grpc, kin-openapi validate) (tools.go:12-23). Notable runtime modules: cobra/viper, chi, robfig/cron/v3, gopsutil, modernc.org/sqlite, pgx, go-redis, moby client, k8s client-go, go-git, aws-sdk-go-v2, Azure/GCP/Alibaba/Vault secret SDKs, OpenTelemetry, grpc, modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk, tailscale.com, aqua (go.mod:5-103). ui/package.json: 50 dependencies + 41 devDependencies (ui/package.json:34-128); npm/dagu/package.json: 1 dependency (tar) + 12 optionalDependencies (platform binaries) (npm/dagu/package.json:33-49); .github/opencode/package.json: 1 CI-fixture dependency (opencode-ai 1.18.11). Lockfiles present: go.sum, ui/pnpm-lock.yaml, npm/dagu/package-lock.json, .github/opencode/package-lock.json.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: supported = main and the latest stable release series, older releases unsupported (SECURITY.md:3-13); report privately to contact@dagu.sh or via GitHub private vulnerability reporting if enabled, no public issues (SECURITY.md:15-23); acknowledgement within 5 business days and status updates at least every 7 days (SECURITY.md:37-43); coordinated disclosure (SECURITY.md:45-47).

claim_checks.claim: Single binary with built-in Web UI, no external database or message broker (README.md:18, 24-25).
claim_checks.evidence: File-backed persistence only: collections map to directories under data_dir (internal/persis/file/backend.go:38-71); run status is appended as JSON lines and fsynced per write (internal/persis/file/dagrun/writer.go:81-104,148-164; dag.json + status.jsonl per run: dagrun/dagrun.go:44-60, attempt.go:42); UI embedded with go:embed (internal/service/frontend/templates.go:30). No DB/broker adapter found for control-plane state; pgx/sqlite/redis in go.mod back step actions (README.md:603-605). Caveat: internal/service/frontend/assets/ is git-ignored (.gitignore:3-4), so a plain `go build ./cmd` has no UI until `make ui` (Makefile:251-253,380-382); release builds run the UI build first (release.yaml:45-53).

claim_checks.claim: Cron scheduling with timezones, overlap policies (skip/all/latest) and catch-up windows (README.md:30, 779-780).
claim_checks.evidence: Code takes precedence over the README wording. Cron via robfig/cron (go.mod:69), TZ=/CRON_TZ= prefixes and @descriptors (specs/063-schedule.md:18-50), one-off RFC3339 schedules and separate stop/restart schedules (internal/service/scheduler/tick_planner.go:636-724). overlap_policy governs catch-up/resume buffers only: the schema says it controls what happens 'when a catchup run is ready but the DAG is still running' (internal/cmn/schema/dag.schema.json:155-160; tick_planner.go:546-612); a live cron tick is always dropped while the DAG is running or queued (tick_planner.go:749-776), so 'all' and 'latest' never queue live ticks. Catch-up: default window 6h comes from the auto-created base.yaml (internal/persis/file/baseconfig/default_base_config.go:52-56; store.go:80-88), replays at most 1000 missed intervals from max(now-window, last tick, last scheduled) (internal/service/scheduler/catchup.go:20-34,54-90), is computed at scheduler start and on resume from pause (tick_planner.go:394-486,1423-1444) and needs queues enabled (tick_planner.go:395-405). Schedules are evaluated on whole-minute ticks and scheduler timing guarantees are outside the conformance suite (specs/063-schedule.md:7-10,45-48).

claim_checks.claim: Zombie detection (default 45s) and a scheduler lock with stale detection for failover (README.md:781, 786).
claim_checks.evidence: Zombie detector default interval 45s, 0 disables (internal/cmn/config/loader.go:1462-1464; internal/service/scheduler/zombie_detector.go:54-56); a run is repaired to failed only after failure_threshold (default 3) consecutive stale heartbeat checks and only if the recorded PID start-time no longer matches a live process (loader.go:1470-1471; zombie_detector.go:210-219,250-285). Proc heartbeat files are written every 5s and go stale after 90s by default (internal/persis/file/proc/store.go:112-117; configurable via proc.* at loader.go:1476-1494), so with defaults a hard-killed local run is marked failed after roughly 3-4 minutes (derived from these constants, not measured). e2e coverage: ui/e2e/zombie-recovery.spec.ts:17-72. Scheduler lock: lock directory under <data>/scheduler/locks with heartbeat and 30s stale threshold (internal/service/scheduler/scheduler.go:207-213; internal/cmn/dirlock/dirlock.go:68-129; loader.go:2045).

claim_checks.claim: Per-step retry with limits, intervals and exit-code filtering; failed runs can be retried (README.md:782, 809-832).
claim_checks.evidence: Step retry_policy supports limit, interval, backoff, max interval and exit-code filter (internal/runtime/node.go:1759-1823; documented in default_base_config.go:109-121). DAG-level auto-retry (internal/ir/dag.go:306-318) is enqueued by a scheduler scan every 30s within a retry window defaulting to 24h (internal/service/scheduler/retry_scanner.go:19,68-90; loader.go:2047); retries are opt-in because steps may be non-idempotent (default_base_config.go:58-62). `dagu retry --run-id [--step] [--downstream]` reuses the run ID: failed/retrying/aborted/rejected nodes and all their descendants are reset and re-run, succeeded upstream nodes keep their status (internal/cmd/retry.go:30-55; internal/runtime/plan.go:449-499). Compensation is left to workflow-defined handlers (README.md:784); no automatic rollback of step side effects was found.

claim_checks.claim: `dagu start-all` runs the server, scheduler, and steps in one process (README.md:199).
claim_checks.evidence: Code takes precedence. Server, scheduler and the default-enabled coordinator share one process (internal/cmd/startall.go:36-45,141-253), but every local DAG run is a separate OS process: the scheduler builds `dagu start ...` and spawns it (internal/service/scheduler/dag_executor.go:305-321; internal/launcher/launcher.go:134-135,457-488) in its own process group (launcher.go:500; internal/cmn/cmdutil/cmd_unix.go:19-25), and step commands are children of that run process (internal/runtime/builtin/command/command.go:105). Scheduler.Stop() stops the planner, queue processor and zombie detector and releases the lock; it does not signal in-flight run processes (internal/service/scheduler/scheduler.go:895-941).

claim_checks.claim: Runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows (README.md:18, 26).
claim_checks.evidence: Release binaries are built for all three (.goreleaser.yaml:14-35), but automated tests run only on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest (ci.yaml:185-189,631-635; conformance.yml:52); macOS appears only as a GOOS=darwin lint (ci.yaml:150) and an npm install smoke test (npm-publish.yaml:277-282). `resources.limits` are unsupported on macOS (internal/runtime/resourcelimit/native_unsupported.go:14-16). WSL2 is not mentioned.

claim_checks.claim: RBAC with five roles under builtin auth; audit logging tracks all actions (README.md:690-700).
claim_checks.evidence: Code takes precedence. The five roles exist (internal/auth/role.go:20-35), but without a license the API rejects creating, updating and deleting users with 'User management requires a Dagu Pro license' (internal/service/frontend/api/v1/api.go:897-901; users.go:107,211,334), LogAudit returns without recording unless the audit feature is licensed (api.go:977-1006; audit endpoints api.go:956-965; terminal/handler.go:111-113), OIDC and trusted-proxy SSO need the sso feature (internal/service/frontend/server.go:655-659) and community API keys are capped at 2 (internal/service/frontend/api/v1/apikeys.go:18,360-379). README.md:205-206 does list RBAC and audit as licensed add-ons, but the Security section states them without that caveat. Default auth mode is builtin (loader.go:668-673).

claim_checks.claim: Built-in MCP server for inspecting workflows and runs and controlling runs (README.md:32, 580).
claim_checks.evidence: A Streamable HTTP MCP handler on modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk is registered at <base>/mcp on every server start, behind the server's auth (internal/service/mcp/server.go:58-65; internal/service/frontend/server.go:896,1345-1363). Tools dagu_read, dagu_change (preview/apply) and dagu_execute (start/enqueue/retry/stop) exist (server.go:26-28,113-154); conformance tests exist (conformance/spec020_mcp_server, spec021, spec022, spec036). No stdio transport. Spec status is inconsistent: specs/020-mcp-server.md:3 'Draft' and specs/README.md:31 'Not implemented' while the endpoint ships.

claim_checks.claim: Queues, concurrency limits and resource limits control how many runs execute at once and where they run (README.md:82).
claim_checks.evidence: max_active_runs is deprecated and ignored for DAG-named local queues (schema default 1; other values only produce a deprecation warning): internal/cmn/schema/dag.schema.json:587-593; internal/spec/dag.go:807-817. Cross-DAG concurrency uses global queues configured in config plus the `queue:` field (dag.schema.json:594-597); worker max_active_runs defaults to 100 (loader.go:2022). `resources.limits` is a per-run CPU/memory cap, not a run-count limiter: cgroup v2 on Linux, needing a writable cgroup under the current one (internal/runtime/resourcelimit/native_linux.go:26-60,80-97), Job Object on Windows (native_windows.go:38-94), unsupported elsewhere including macOS (native_unsupported.go:14-16); enforcement is best-effort and only warns when it cannot be applied (resourcelimit/guard.go:43-67; internal/runtime/builtin/command/command.go:116-120).

claim_checks.claim: A single machine can run thousands of workflow runs per day (README.md:81).
claim_checks.evidence: No throughput benchmark, load test or published result exists in the repo, and the README gives no hardware, workload or method. Only 9 Go Benchmark functions exist, in 5 test files (internal/cmn/stringutil/hash_test.go, internal/service/auth/service_test.go, internal/persis/store/distributed_test.go, internal/persis/file/dagrun/latest_attempt_external_test.go, internal/persis/file/dagrun/attempt_test.go), with no results published. The docs site (docs.dagu.sh) is outside the checkout.

risks: Licence-gated features inside the GPL code base: without a licence key the API rejects user create/update/delete ('User management requires a Dagu Pro license', internal/service/frontend/api/v1/api.go:897-901; users.go:107,211,334), records no audit entries (api.go:977-1006), disables OIDC/trusted-proxy SSO (internal/service/frontend/server.go:655-659), blocks incident management (api.go:967-975) and caps API keys at 2 (apikeys.go:18,360-379). The README's Security section presents five roles and audit logging without this caveat (README.md:690-700 vs 205-206).

Licensing: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSING.md:3). Importing the experimental embedded Go API into a distributed binary triggers GPL obligations, and proprietary embedding is routed to a separate commercial licence (LICENSING.md:7-13). Licence metadata is inconsistent across files: README 'GNU GPLv3' (README.md:1119), npm and OpenAPI 'GPL-3.0' (npm/dagu/package.json:25; api/v1/api.yaml:10-12, which links a LICENSE.md that does not exist), ui/package.json 'SEE LICENSE.md' (ui/package.json:29).

Platform coverage: no macOS test job in CI (ci.yaml:185-189,631-635; conformance.yml:52), `resources.limits` unsupported on macOS (internal/runtime/resourcelimit/native_unsupported.go:14-16), WSL2 undocumented (no mention in repo), and data/log directories come from adrg/xdg DataHome while config is fixed to ~/.config (internal/cmn/config/loader.go:185-188), so macOS paths may differ from README defaults (library behaviour not verified).

Process-tree containment on Unix is process-group based: step commands start with Setpgid and stop is kill(-pgid) (internal/cmn/cmdutil/cmd_unix.go:19-25; lifecycle_unix.go:33-57); cgroups are used only for CPU/memory caps, not for killing (resourcelimit/native_linux.go:62-67) and no subreaper/cgroup.kill logic was found in internal/, so descendants that leave the group are outside these signals. Stop is a graceful signal then forced kill after max_clean_up_time_sec, default 5s (internal/runtime/agent/agent.go:2267-2341; internal/ir/dag.go:505-519); a DAG/step timeout force-kills immediately with exit code 124 (internal/runtime/builtin/command/command.go:132-140). Scheduler shutdown does not signal in-flight runs (scheduler.go:895-941); hard-killed runs are recovered by heartbeat staleness, roughly 3-4 minutes with defaults (derived from proc/store.go:112-117 and loader.go:1462-1471).

Scheduling defaults: the auto-created base.yaml is inherited by all DAGs and sets catchup_window 6h, overlap_policy skip, hist_retention_days 30, max_active_steps 10, max_clean_up_time_sec 5 (internal/persis/file/baseconfig/default_base_config.go:11-56; store.go:80-88). A scheduler restart can replay up to 1000 missed runs per DAG inside the window (internal/service/scheduler/catchup.go:31-34), while retries are opt-in because steps may be non-idempotent (default_base_config.go:58-62). Live ticks that fire while a run is active or queued are silently dropped regardless of overlap_policy (tick_planner.go:749-776). Scheduler timing/dispatch guarantees are explicitly outside the conformance suite (specs/063-schedule.md:7-10).

Network and security defaults: the server's automatic update check to api.github.com is on by default and not mentioned in the README (loader.go:2009; internal/service/frontend/server.go:916; config.schema.json:37-41); `start-all` enables the coordinator gRPC listener on 127.0.0.1:50055 with plaintext h2c by default (loader.go:1320,2017-2019,2050); the Docker image runs as user `dagu` with passwordless sudo and DAGU_HOST=0.0.0.0 (Dockerfile:105-112,123); container steps need Docker daemon access that the README says grants control of the host daemon (README.md:132-135); steps run with a filtered environment, so variables outside the allowlist (for example HTTP_PROXY or AWS_*) are not forwarded unless configured (internal/cmn/config/env.go:23-33; env_unix.go:16-49).

Packaging and supply chain: the README installer is fetched from the main branch and verifies only a SHA-256 taken from the same release's checksums.txt (README.md:105; scripts/installer.sh:1520-1536); the build-provenance attestation step is continue-on-error and the installer does not check it (release.yaml:67-71); no GPG/cosign signing or SBOM generation found for binaries or images; the npm postinstall fallback downloads a tarball from registry.npmjs.org without a separate checksum (npm/dagu/install.js:81-117); the Dockerfile temporarily disables apt signature checks to install ubuntu-keyring (Dockerfile:41-61); the Helm chart's default image tag is appVersion 2.11.1 (charts/dagu/Chart.yaml:6; values.yaml:15-16; templates/_helpers.tpl:46), inside the range the README calls broken for scoped notification routing (README.md:764); a plain `go build`/`go install` produces a binary without the Web UI (.gitignore:3-4).

Maturity and scope: large, fast-moving surface (33 CLI commands, 230 REST operations, 544 Go modules, Go 1.27.0 toolchain required: cmd/main.go:36-68; api/v1/api.yaml; go.mod:3). specs/README.md:13-77 lists 63 specs of which 32 are Implemented, 29 Partially implemented and 2 Not implemented (including the MCP endpoint contract, which ships). The embedded Go API is 'experimental and may change' (doc.go:7-8; README.md:1047). Security fixes are provided only for main and the latest stable series (SECURITY.md:5-11). Public documentation lives off-repo (docs.dagu.sh), so doc-site claims could not be verified here.
